template: In {period}, {p} of {agency}'s new contracts above the small-purchase threshold ({n} of {N}; {d} of {D}) were awarded without competition.

Agencies record for each contract whether it was competed. We count new contracts marked 'not competed' or 'not available for competition'. We leave out small purchases: contracts handled under simplified procedures, or worth $250,000 or less, the federal small-purchase threshold. Contracting offices give a reason for each non-competitive award, such as a single possible supplier, urgency or utilities. These codes are as reported by the contracting office and can be wrong; they don't show intent.
The largest single award, {amount} to {recipient} ({reason}), is {share} of FY{t}'s not-competed dollars; the five largest are listed below.
Some sole-source awards are authorized by law, such as those to small businesses in the SBA's 8(a) program, which includes Alaska Native corporations.
Business categories are as reported on each contract and can overlap (a firm can be in several), so they aren't added together.
Organization type is reported consistently only from FY{first}, so earlier years aren't shown.

In the complete years FY{first} to FY{last_complete}, the share of new contract dollars awarded without competition ranged from {min_pct} (FY{min_fy}) to {max_pct} (FY{max_fy}). {period} is {cur_pct}.
Awarding a contract without competition is often lawful; this doesn't indicate anything improper.
